convoLines.text: "I've gotten good at reading faces. Out here, faces say what words won't."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Jesse shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the east treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Now — Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"Still on whether they can trust you."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Benjamin owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Sleep's gone strange. I tend the fire without being asked at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
You show them Goldenrod — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Nobody says Benjamin's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"I dreamed Jorge was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About that question — Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
Their tone levels out — courteous, careful, further away.
"Still on whether you've hurt someone!"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Jorge always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Pokeweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Jesse sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Duel. They just... took Rosa. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Same as always: we endure."
"Still on what's been happening."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"You told me yes, once. No details. I haven't forgotten. I just don't ask."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took me. Duel — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

d41: The village's quarrel was with Benjamin — and Benjamin is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
